intended_object: The Sobolev space W^{1,p}_0(Ω): the closure of the test functions C_c^∞(Ω) in W^{1,p}(Ω), for an open set Ω in a finite-dimensional real inner product space with Lebesgue (Haar) measure and 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞ (Evans §5.2). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
How the space is built:
- `W1p mu Omega p` is the closed subspace of `Lp (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E)) p (mu.restrict Omega)` made of value–gradient jets (u, g) that satisfy the weak integration-by-parts identity ∫_Ω (∂_v φ · u + φ · ⟨v, g⟩) = 0 for every test function φ ∈ 𝓓(Ω) and every direction v.
- The jet norm is the Lᵖ norm of (|u|² + |∇u|²)^{1/2}. This is equivalent to the usual W^{1,p} norm (‖u‖_p + ‖∇u‖_p), so it gives the same topology and the same closures.
- `W1p.ofTestFunctionₗ` sends φ to (φ, ∇φ). It is linear and injective.
- `w1p0Submodule` is the topological closure of its range, and `W1p0` is the underlying submodule.

This is exactly the textbook definition of W^{1,p}_0(Ω) as the closure of C_c^∞(Ω) in W^{1,p}(Ω).

Edge cases: the textbook usually takes p < ∞. For p = ∞ the construction still gives the closure, which is a standard (if rarely used) convention, so this is not an error.

Generality:
- The setting is a finite-dimensional real inner product space with an additive Haar measure. This is the natural setting for Sobolev spaces on open subsets of ℝⁿ: the inner product is needed to represent the derivative as a gradient, and the Haar measure is Lebesgue measure.
- The functions are scalar-valued, which is the standard notion.

Mathlib comparison: Mathlib's only Sobolev-type notion is `MemSobolev`, the Bessel-potential spaces H^{s,p} on the whole space, defined via tempered distributions. Mathlib has no W^{1,p}(Ω) or W^{1,p}_0(Ω) on open sets, so this definition is not too narrow.
